name: How to Plan a Bathroom Flooring Replacement Without Subfloor Surprises

step.name: Step 1: Pull existing fixtures and strip out old floor coverings
step.text: Disconnect and remove the toilet, vanity, and base trim to reveal the entire floor surface. Strip away the existing tile or vinyl completely so you can directly inspect what lies underneath rather than laying new material over questionable subflooring.

step.name: Step 2: Inspect subfloor integrity and check moisture readings
step.text: Examine the plywood or concrete for active leaks, dark water stains, soft spots, and rot around the toilet flange and tub edge. Take accurate moisture readings and verify the surface is structurally sound and level before introducing new adhesives or underlayments.

step.name: Step 3: Repair damaged wood and install the appropriate underlayment
step.text: Cut out and replace any rotted subflooring, ensuring the remaining framing is rigid and adequately fastened to eliminate floor flex. Fasten an approved cement backer board, uncoupling membrane, or waterproof underlayment according to manufacturer specifications for your chosen surface material.

step.name: Step 4: Dry-fit materials and establish your layout lines
step.text: Map out your starting points, transitions at the doorway, and cuts around heating registers and plumbing pipes. Dry-fitting porcelain tiles or measuring sheet vinyl carefully prevents awkward slivers along visible walls and ensures seamless coverage.

step.name: Step 5: Set the flooring and seal all plumbing penetrations
step.text: Lay your tile with proper thin-set mortar or roll out your sheet vinyl using bathroom-rated adhesive, pressing firmly for complete bond contact. Finish with manufacturer-approved grout or heat seams, and apply flexible waterproof sealant around all pipe penetrations and perimeter expansion gaps.
